# Sirach Chapter 20 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 20 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_020_page_001.jpg

---

**20:1** Some rebukes come at exactly the wrong time; and sometimes staying silent is the wisest thing.

**20:2** Better to correct someone directly than to seethe with anger; the person who admits fault avoids failure.

**20:3** A forced act of virtue is like a eunuch trying to violate a young woman — it makes no sense.

**20:4** Some people stay silent because they have nothing to say; others stay silent because they know when to speak.

**20:5** The wise person waits for the right moment; the braggart and fool opens their mouth at the wrong time.

**20:6** Someone who never shuts up is a nuisance; someone who grabs authority that isn't theirs is resented.

**20:7** In misfortune, there can be an unexpected windfall; in loss, there can be gain.

**20:8** Some gifts bring you no benefit; others come back to you doubled.

**20:9** Sometimes humiliation leads to glory; some people rise up from the lowest place.

**20:10** Some people buy a lot for very little but end up paying seven times what it's worth.

**20:11** A wise person earns affection by how they speak; but eloquent words wasted on fools are wasted.

**20:12** A gift from a fool does you no good — he's watching every angle where you thought he had none.

**20:13** He gives a little and complains a lot; he announces his gifts like a town crier. Who could possibly feel grateful for that?

**20:14** Today this man borrows, tomorrow he's back asking again — God and everyone else can't stand such a person.

**20:15** A fool says, "I have no friends and nobody appreciates what I do for them" — but the people who eat his bread say mean things about him.

**20:16** How many people will laugh at him, and how often?

**20:17** Better to trip on the floor than to trip over your tongue; the downfall of the wicked comes just as fast.

**20:18** A graceless person is like a story told at the wrong time — it keeps coming up in the mouths of uneducated people.

**20:19** A proverb quoted by a fool falls flat — because he says it at the wrong moment.

**20:20** Some people are kept from sinning by nothing more than lack of opportunity; when they rest, they feel no guilt.

**20:21** Some people are ruined by their own timidity — destroyed by a foolish decision.

**20:22** Some people make a pledge out of friendship and end up making an enemy for no reason.

**20:23** A lie puts a stain on the person; a constant critic's blame becomes just noise.

**20:24** A lie is an ugly mark on a person; it's always on the lips of the ignorant.

**20:25** Better a thief than a confirmed liar — but both are on their way to ruin.

**20:26** Dishonor belongs to the liar; his shame never goes away.

**20:27** A wise person gets ahead through what they say; a prudent person knows how to please those in authority.

**20:28** Work the land and the harvest piles up; please those in power and you can make amends for wrongs done.

**20:29** Gifts and bribes blind even the wise; they work like a gag that stops a rebuker's mouth.

**20:30** Wisdom kept hidden, treasure buried out of sight — what good are either of them?

**20:31** Better to hide your foolishness than to hide your wisdom.
